title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow. Using a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine) we produced one shared initial candidate per task via gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated the same candidate under both conditions. A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforced structured workflow policies and could trigger ≤1 repair iteration per guarded episode. Observed outcomes: baseline success = 120/120; guarded success = 120/120; contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces report repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. We refine the experimental framing, provide a compact formal definition of the binary outcome used in inference, present a nearest-work comparison that situates this study, and give artifact-grounded methodological recommendations for follow-up confirmatory designs when generator outputs are frequently invalid.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) can map operator intent to concrete configuration commands, but syntactically plausible outputs may violate stateful workflow invariants (for example, performing an uplink switchover without make-before-break sequencing). Prior work therefore recommends tool-augmentation: verification, emulation, digital twins, or veto layers that detect semantic failures visible only in closed-loop execution. Our study isolates the marginal effect of such a validator+repair subsystem on identical generator outputs by using a shared-generation paired design: for each preregistered task we produced one generator candidate (shared_initial) and scored it both as baseline (LLM-only suggestion) and as guarded (validator ± bounded repair). The central confirmatory question (preregistered) was: Does integrating an executable network emulator as a validator in a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce semantic/network-level failures when enacting LLM-generated configuration changes compared to an LLM-only suggestion workflow? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered paired experiment (N=120) that holds the generator fixed to isolate validator/repair effects; (2) a concise formalization of the binary success/failure label used for the confirmatory McNemar test; (3) an artifact-grounded report of a degenerate ceiling outcome (100% success in both conditions) with exact statistics and reconciliation; and (4) targeted methodological recommendations for future confirmatory designs that aim to exercise repair behavior.
sections.related_work: Executable, emulation-based benchmarks and verification tools demonstrate that closed-loop tests reveal sequencing and stateful errors beyond token-level checks. Representative efforts include NetConfArena (closed-loop executable benchmark; arXiv:2608.23179), recent benchmarking of LLM-driven configuration repair (arXiv:2604.22513), and tool/agent architectures advocating guarded tool use and bounded autonomy (surveys and prototypes summarized in the archival evidence). These works collectively motivate generate→validate→repair architectures but differ in experimental lens: many prior studies compare generators across task banks (generator-focused) or present integrated toolboxes without isolating validator marginal effects. Nearest-work comparison (compact): - Protogeros et al., Benchmarking LLM-Driven Network Configuration Repair (arXiv:2604.22513): benchmarked repair behavior and failure modes; emphasis on generator and repair but typically not a paired shared-generation isolation. - NetConfArena (arXiv:2608.23179): executable closed-loop benchmark exposing semantic failures at enactment time. - MeshAgent (DOI:10.1145/3771567): practical system-level proposal for reliable LLM-assisted network management. How this study differs: we use a shared-generation paired design (one shared candidate per task), a deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) that enforces structured task-encoded workflow policies, a strict repair budget (≤1 repair iteration per guarded episode), and a single hosted generator model (gpt-5-mini). The paired shared-candidate lens isolates validator/repair marginal effects but can under-exercise repair when the generator is well-calibrated for the selected task bank.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) before execution. Design: paired-binary confirmatory test with N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks partitioned deterministically into three topology classes (edge/core/leaf–spine; 40 tasks each). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Prespecified test: exact two-sided McNemar; paired bootstrap-percentile 95% CI computed with 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729. Execution contract enforced deterministic emulator resets, contamination heuristics, and an explicit exclusion/missingness plan; no technical exclusions occurred. Task generation and payloads. Tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task manifest includes initial_state, expected_final_state, natural-language intent, and an explicit required_sequence (ordered canonical operations) plus difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). Generator and harness. A single shared-generation stage produced one candidate per task using declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; model_calls_used = 120). Each candidate was evaluated under two scoring episodes: baseline (LLM-only suggestion scored/validated but no repair applied) and guarded (validator executed the candidate and invoked at most one repair when validator.violation_count>0). Validator and scoring rule (formal binary outcome). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0). Scoring rule used to produce the binary label (success/pass vs failure) for the confirmatory test is the following artifact-grounded decision logic: an episode is labeled successful (pass = 1) when the scorer reports score_reason_code == "VALID_CONFIGURATION" AND validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true AND validator_trace.violation_count == 0. An episode is labeled failing (pass = 0) when the scorer returns a non-valid verdict (for example validator_trace.violation_count > 0) or when the scorer signals a non-completion under the harness exclusion rules. Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json) exemplify the mapping (e.g., score_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION", violation_count = 0 => pass). Repair policy and instrumentation. The guarded repair policy invoked at most one repair iteration when violation_count>0; repair prompts and repair_provider_trace artifacts were archived when generated. The harness recorded provider-call audits, deterministic emulator resets (container checksums and seeds), contamination checks (duplicate-output detection and cache-key reuse), and produced deterministic_reconciliation artifacts. Statistical analysis. Primary test: exact two-sided McNemar on paired binary pass/fail labels. Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI computed by resampling paired outcomes (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Secondary and sensitivity analyses (prespecified) handle excluded pairs and alternative failure codings; none applied because there were zero exclusions.
sections.results: Execution and primary outcomes. The run completed with planned_episode_count = 240 and completed_episode_count = 240; no technical exclusions (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). The shared-generation stage produced one candidate per pair (model_calls_used = 120; stage_counts recorded as shared_initial_generation = 120). Condition-level summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0 (success rates = 1.0 for both). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0; observed paired-difference = 0.00. Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. Repair activity: validator_trace.repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes; consequently no repair_provider_trace artifacts were generated. Per-topology counts (extracted from representative scoring artifacts and the task manifest): Edge (40 pairs): baseline 40/40, guarded 40/40; Core (40): baseline 40/40, guarded 40/40; Leaf–spine (40): baseline 40/40, guarded 40/40. Representative diagnostic artifact example. A typical scoring artifact (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json) shows normalized_response == normalized_reference_answer, validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true, parsed_command_count == required_command_count, validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, validator_version = 5.0, and score_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION". Contamination and reconciliation. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty; deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms provider-call audits (hosted_model_call_event_count = 120, cache_miss_count = 120, cross-condition cache reuse = false) and consistent pair accounting (complete_pair_count = 120). These artifacts underpin the reported contingency table and exact-test results.
sections.discussion: Interpretation of the ceiling outcome. The shared-generation paired design isolates the marginal effect of the validator and bounded repair policy by removing generator variance across paired episodes. In the archived task bank and under the frozen prompt/declared model, the shared initial candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in every pair; therefore the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to exercise repair and could not reduce semantic failures relative to the baseline. Statistically, zero discordant pairs (n_10 = n_01 = 0) produce a degenerate bootstrap CI and an exact McNemar p = 1.0; this is an expected consequence of the observed concordant data under the preregistered analysis and resampling scheme. Design trade-offs and recommendations for future confirmatory runs. The paired shared-candidate design provides clear internal control for validator marginal effects but reduces the chance to observe repair if the generator is well-calibrated. Artifact-grounded recommendations (deriveable from task_manifest difficulty fields and archived traces): (1) Allow independent per-condition generation for a prespecified subset (paired blocking retained where appropriate) so guarded arms can intercept generator errors arising from sampling or prompt perturbations. (2) Stratify confirmatory power on high-difficulty tasks (for example tasks with difficulty.level == "very_hard" or dependency_rule_count ≥ 2 in the manifest) to increase generator-induced violation incidence. (3) Prespecify controlled prompt perturbations (the preregistration included exploratory perturbation plans) on a deterministic subset to elevate generator error rates while preserving other paired comparisons. (4) For exploratory arms, allow a larger repair budget (≥1) to measure repair convergence and repair-call costs. Operational and audit implications. Even when unused, a deterministic validator that emits structured traces (validation_before/after, violation codes, touched fields) supports operator auditability, post-hoc analysis, and independent review. The archived artifacts demonstrate end-to-end instrumented accounting (provider-call audits, validator traces, deterministic_reconciliation) that can serve operator-facing explanations and third-party audits. Threats to validity. Internal validity is strong (deterministic provisioning, zero exclusions, complete provider-call audits). Construct validity is limited by validator policy encodings based on synthetic task payloads (the validator enforces required_sequence and workflow_policies but does not model all vendor-specific behaviors). External validity is constrained by the synthetic deterministic task corpus, a single hosted generator (gpt-5-mini), and a single frozen prompting strategy. Conclusion validity: the preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline failure ≈0.40 and targeted an absolute reduction of 0.15; observed baseline = 0.00 violates those assumptions and renders the confirmatory test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) that compared an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline to an LLM-only workflow using a shared-generation paired design and a deterministic emulator validator. All 120 shared initial candidates passed the validator in both conditions (n_11 = 120), yielding a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The principal scientific contribution is methodological: a preregistered, artifact-rich paired protocol cleanly isolates validator/repair marginal effects and produces deterministic archival artifacts (task manifests, validator traces, provider-call audits, reconciliation files) that enable reproducible failure analysis and transparent auditing even when the primary confirmatory test is degenerate. Archived artifacts permit follow-up studies that relax shared-generation, compare generator families, expand repair budgets, and focus on production-rooted corpora to quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
